resources.string: A code is any QR code you print or already own. A handshake step that asks you to scan a code is passed by one of the codes registered here. Only a fingerprint of each code is kept on this phone, never the code itself. A code you already own should not hold a secret, such as a Wi-Fi password; a code made here is the safest choice.
“%1$s” is deleted from COMMAND, and a step that asks for a code no longer accepts it. The printed code itself does not change. This cannot be undone.
This phone has no camera, so QR codes cannot be used on it. A step that asks for a code asks you to type a phrase instead.
To scan a code, COMMAND needs Android to give it the camera.
Android has not given COMMAND the camera, so a code cannot be scanned. You can allow it in the app\'s settings.
Turn on the camera consent above to add a code.
Name for the code, such as Kitchen
Point the camera at the code you want to register as “%1$s”.
Camera view. Point it at the code to register.
Print this or show it on another screen, then scan it to register it
A new QR code to print or show on another screen
Registered “%1$s”. A step that asks for a code accepts it now.
That code holds no text, so it cannot be used. Try another code.
That code is already registered, as “%1$s”.
%1$d codes are registered, the most there can be. Delete one to add another.
The camera could not be used. If another app is using it, close that app and try again.
